# v1.3.3 — Performance & stability hardening

## What changed

### Server hot paths

- **Bounded caches.** The in-memory caches that backed chapter and API lookups
  now have hard size caps, so long-running sessions can no longer grow them
  without limit.
- **SQLite tuned for reads.** Added the missing indexes plus sensible pragmas
  and a prepared-statement cache, cutting repeated query overhead on the
  hot paths.
- **`/api/health` under control.** Health checks now run with bounded
  concurrency so a burst of probes can't stampede the process.
- **Crash safety.** Express error middleware catches async route failures, and
  an `uncaughtException` handler logs and exits with `process.exit(1)` instead
  of leaving the server in a broken state. Request bodies are capped at 6mb.
- **Cheaper logging.** Log writes are batched instead of flushing on every
  line.

### Downloads

- **The queue is now O(N) instead of O(N²).** Enqueue/dequeue no longer rescan
  the whole queue on every operation.
- **Real cancellation.** Cancelling a download actually stops its in-flight
  work rather than letting it finish in the background.
- **500-chapter clamp.** A single batch is clamped to 500 chapters so one
  request can't pin the queue.

### Client runtime

- **Reader scrolling is smooth.** Scroll handling is coalesced through
  `requestAnimationFrame` and layout measurements are cached.
- **No more listener leaks.** Event listeners are properly torn down when
  views are replaced.
- **API traffic deduped and bounded.** Identical in-flight requests are
  deduped, the client cache has a size cap, and retries are capped.
- **Lazy modules.** `tts.js` loads on demand.

### Startup weight & offline

- **Lighter boot.** The render-blocking Tesseract CDN script is gone, `marked`
  is deferred, and an unused OpenCV inpaint worker was dropped.
- **Safer service worker.** The dynamic cache is bounded and an offline shell
  fallback serves when the network is unavailable.

### OTA durability

- **Staging dirs are pruned and installs are serialized**, so an interrupted or
  concurrent update can't leave partial state behind.

## Notes

- No user-facing feature changes; this release is about keeping the app fast and
  stable under load and over long sessions.
- Adds 8 regression test files guarding the caches, queue limits, logger
  batching, OTA cleanup and service-worker behaviour.

# v1.3.2 — App Store Library & Search rework

## What changed

### Library

- **The Library now looks like the Apple App Store** in the App Store themes
  (`App Store (Light Glass)` and `App Store (Dark Glass)`).
- **Bookmarks** are a grouped inset list instead of a card grid: cover
  thumbnail, title, a subtitle with your chapter and progress, a thin accent
  progress bar, and a chevron. A "New" pill marks titles with fresh chapters,
  and an offline count appears when chapters are saved offline.
- **History** gets the same treatment, grouped under day headers (Today,
  Yesterday, This Week, Earlier) with iOS section headings.
- **Every control was restyled**: an iOS search field, plain text toolbar
  buttons (Sort / Select, with Select switching to Done), an iOS popover sort
  menu with a blue check on the active option, pill category chips, an iOS
  bottom selection toolbar, and refined empty states.

### Search

- **Search now looks and behaves like App Store search** in the App Store
  themes.
- The pill **Search button is replaced by a live field**: results update as you
  type (debounced), with an iOS **Cancel** button that clears the query and
  returns to the suggested view.
- The idle view is a **Suggested** surface: your **Recent** searches as an
  inset list (tap to re-run) and **Browse by Genre** as 2-up iOS category
  tiles.
- **Results** render as an iOS **inset list** (cover thumbnail, title,
  type/genre subtitle, chevron) instead of a card grid. The genre browser's
  results use the same list.

## Notes

- This rework is **scoped to the App Store themes**. The default Dark and
  Light themes keep the original Library grid/toolbar and the pill-button +
  card-grid search, unchanged.
- Switching themes while the Library or Search view is open re-renders it live.

# v1.3.1 — Themed milestone badges & Library/History crash fix

## What changed

- **Milestone badges got a lot harder.** The lifetime ladder now starts at
  **100 chapters** and climbs steeply: **100, 500, 1250, 2500, 5000 and
  10000**. The early easy tiers are gone, so a badge actually means something.
- **Every badge has its own icon.** No more generic checkmarks. Each tier now
  shows a distinct icon, and **each naming theme has its own icon set** — Murim
  shows swords and flames, Mage shows wands and stars, Hunter shows eyes and
  lightning, and so on.
- **A colour ramp for the tiers.** Badges climb through **bronze, silver, gold,
  platinum, diamond and mythic** colours, so your progress is readable at a
  glance. Locked badges stay dimmed until you earn them.

## Fixes

- **Fixed a crash in the Library.** Opening the Library could throw
  `librarylastdata is not defined` and leave the page blank. The library's
  filter, sort, offline-status and multi-select state are now properly declared.
- **Fixed a crash in History.** The history search box threw
  `historysearchterm is not defined`. History search now works again.

## Under the hood

- The milestone module exposes a `TIER_RAMP`, a per-theme `THEME_ICONS` map and
  an `iconSvg()` helper that emits inline SVG (icons inherit the badge colour
  via `currentColor`).
- Milestone and account tests updated for the new thresholds, tiers and icons.

# v1.3.0 — Account rework, Chapter Milestones & rank titles

## What changed

- **A brand-new Account page.** The old wall of stacked panels is gone. Account
  now opens with a **hero header** showing your current rank, chapters read and
  day streak, with a progress bar toward your next milestone. Everything below
  is grouped into clean, **collapsible sections** so the page stays short and
  scannable.
- **Chapter Milestones.** Nine lifetime tiers (1, 10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500,
  1000, 2500 chapters) turn your reading into badges. Unlocked tiers light up;
  locked ones show how far you have to go. Your current tier is highlighted.
- **Choose your title naming.** Rank names adapt to the genre you love. Pick
  from **Classic, Murim, Fantasy, Knight, Mage, Cultivation** or **Hunter** —
  so 500 chapters reads as "Sage" in Classic, "Grandmaster" in Murim, "A-Rank"
  in Hunter, and so on.
- **Goals.** Set a **chapter-count goal** and a **weekly goal**, each with its
  own progress bar. Goals are saved on your device and update as you read.
- **Streak badges.** Consecutive-day reading streaks now unlock badges at 3, 7,
  14, 30 and 100 days.
- **Richer stats.** The Reading Stats panel now shows a **14-day activity
  sparkline**, plus **top sources** and **top genres** as ranked bars, and an
  in-progress / completed summary.

## Fixes

- Account buttons are consistent again: they no longer use near-black fills that
  clashed with the theme, they meet a comfortable tap-target size, and their
  labels are no longer forced to uppercase. Dark, Light and App Store themes all
  share the same clean styling.
- Account panels no longer inherit the reader's bottom-sheet sizing (which had
  capped them at 500px wide with their own scrollbar), so cards now size to
  their content.

## Under the hood

- New pure module `public/js/milestones.js` computes tiers, ranks, streaks and
  goal progress. Everything is **derived** from the existing `chapter_reads`
  log — no new database tables.
- `/api/user/stats` gained a `dailyReads` series (last 14 days) to power the
  sparkline.
- Added a milestones unit test and an account-rework guard test.

# v1.2.21 — A simpler, four-tab app

## What changed

- **Four tabs, nothing more.** The bottom navigation is now just **Home**,
  **Search**, **Library** and **Account**. Two tabs have been retired and the
  app is clearer and faster to get around.
- **Packs are gone.** The Packs feature — curated collections, its detail view
  and the pack progress/ordering tools — has been removed entirely. Curated
  reading lists are no longer part of the app.
- **Novels now live on Home.** The full Novels block — with its **Classic
  Literature** and **Popular Books** sub-tabs and its own search box — has
  moved onto the Home screen. You get the same catalogue without leaving Home.
- **No more duplicate carousels.** The old "Popular Novels" and "Classic
  Literature" carousels on Home have been removed, since the Novels block now
  covers both.

## Under the hood

- Deleted the pack data layer (`packs-data.js`), the pack generation script and
  the pack-powered Daily Event drawer.
- Removed all pack view markup, styles and JavaScript, plus the retired Novels
  and Pack navigation tabs and their views.
- Home renders the Novels block in place, wired to the existing classics and
  popular grids.
- Updated the regression tests and added a guard that keeps the bottom nav at
  four tabs and confirms the Pack feature stays removed.

# v1.2.20 — Top Charts & simpler feedback

## What changed

- **App Store "Top Charts".** If you use the App Store (Glass) theme, Rankings
  now looks and behaves like the real App Store charts: a clean, numbered
  vertical list — rank, cover thumbnail, title, subtitle and the ranking metric
  on the right — grouped into an iOS-style inset list with hairline separators.
  The type filters became an iOS segmented control and the criterion picker an
  iOS select. Dark and Light themes keep the existing card grid, unchanged.
- **Rankings on Home, full charts in their own view.** Home now shows a compact
  **Top 5 preview**. Tap **See All** to open the full **Top Charts** view with
  every criterion (Most Popular, Trending, Top Rated, Most Read, Longest,
  Shortest, Newest, Recently Updated, Best Matches, Most Downloaded, A–Z,
  Completed), type filters, the "My reads" toggle and endless scrolling.
- **No more disliking.** The thumbs-down button is gone. Recommendations are
  driven purely by what you actually read and bookmark, so nothing gets
  silently hidden. (The underlying signal storage is kept dormant for a future
  explicit "Like".)

## Under the hood

- Removed the dislike hard-veto and the dislike weighting from
  `server/recommendation-engine.js`; explicit **likes** still boost titles.
- Rankings rendering is now theme-aware: App Store themes get the numbered
  Top Charts list (`.chart-row`), other themes get the card grid.
- Switching themes re-renders the rankings immediately, so the presentation
  always matches the active theme.
- The full Top Charts list lives in a dedicated `#view-rankings` view with its
  own pagination and infinite scroll.
- Kept `user_signals` table and the `POST/GET /api/user/signals` endpoints
  intact but unused by the UI, ready for a future Like feature.
- Updated the engine, rankings-view and App Store theme test suites.

# v1.2.19 — Smarter recommendations + Rankings

## What changed

- **A real recommendation engine.** The "Recommended for You" shelf used to just
  count the genres of your last few reads. It now builds a weighted interest
  profile from everything you do — what you read, how deep you read, how
  recently, and what you bookmark — then scores every candidate title against it.
  Recommendations span **manhwa, manga, manhua, novels, classics and print
  books**, not just one genre.
- **More shelves.** Instead of a single row you now get several, each explained:
  *Recommended for You*, *Because you read …*, *More {your favorite genre}*, and
  a *For Manhwa/Novel Readers* shelf. Each card can carry a small "why" chip
  (e.g. "More Action", "Because you read Solo Leveling").
- **Rankings, right on the Home screen.** A new **Rankings** section ranks the
  whole catalogue and lets you pick the criterion yourself: Most Popular,
  Trending Now, Top Rated, Most Read, Longest, Shortest, Newest, Recently
  Updated, Best Matches, Most Downloaded, A–Z, and Completed Only. Filter by
  content type (Manhwa, Manga, Manhua, Novels, Classics, Print) and, for
  "Most Read", switch between your own activity and a global proxy.
- **Tell us what you don't want.** Every rankings card has a thumbs-down button.
  It is remembered locally and quietly pushes similar titles down in your
  recommendations.
- **Honest numbers.** Most sources do not publish real view or rating counts, so
  ranking metrics are clearly labelled as estimates — never invented precision.

## Under the hood

- New pure module `server/recommendation-engine.js` (profile, scoring, ranking,
  explanations) with its own unit tests.
- New endpoints: `GET /api/recommend`, `GET /api/rankings`,
  `GET /api/rankings/criteria`, and `POST/GET /api/user/signals`.
- New derived cache table `title_signals` (rebuilt from your bookmarks, history
  and read log) plus an optional `user_signals` table for thumbs up/down. Both
  are created automatically and backfilled on first launch.
- **Richer rankings data.** Chapter counts and series status only live on each
  title's detail page, so metadata-based rankings (Longest, Shortest, Top Rated,
  Completed) now hydrate those fields once and store them in a new `title_meta`
  cache. Results get sharper after the first launch and stay correct offline.
- **Rankings paginate.** The list loads 24 at a time and keeps absolute ranks
  (page 2 starts at #25) as you scroll.
- **Fixed a caching bug** that stopped listing-style responses (rankings,
  recommendations) from ever being cached, forcing every visit to re-fetch from
  providers. Repeat loads are now instant.
- Tests: `tests/recommendation-engine.test.js`, `tests/rankings-view.test.js`,
  `tests/title-signals.test.js`.

# v1.2.18 — App Store buttons + icons

## What changed

- **New App Store icons** — the bottom nav (Home, Pack, Novels, Search, Library,
  Account) now uses crisp SF Symbols-style glyphs when an App Store theme is
  active. The original icons are unchanged for the Dark and Light themes.
- **Every button got the iOS treatment** — the search field and its button, the
  library toolbar, reader controls, carousel arrows, close buttons, and dialog
  buttons are now rounded pills and circular fills in the App Store look.
- **Cleaner arrows and controls** — the carousel arrows, zoom and close controls
  use proper icon shapes instead of plain text symbols.

## Under the hood

- The icon swap and button pass are scoped to the App Store themes only, so the
  default Dark theme and the Light theme render exactly as before.

# v1.2.17 — A cleaner reader

## What changed

- **Reader scrollbar removed** — the scroll indicator that appeared on the
  right edge of the reader is gone. Chapters still scroll exactly as before,
  the bar just no longer shows while you read.

## Under the hood

- The reader view hides its scrollbar on both Chromium/Android (WebKit) and
  Firefox, so the page is edge-to-edge with no stray track or accent thumb.

# v1.2.16 — Every source back online

## Providers that were down are back (or gone)

A full sweep of every source found a handful that had rotted: some had moved to
a new domain, some had been rebuilt as client-only apps, and some had simply
shut down. This release repairs what can be repaired and retires what cannot.

## What changed

- **MangaKakalot** — rebuilt for its new home, `mangakakalot.fun`. Search,
  Popular, Latest, details and **full chapter readers** all work again. The
  reader fetches its page list from the site's GraphQL API and decrypts it
  locally (AES-256-GCM), so complete chapters load instead of a 6-image
  preview. Chapter numbers are taken from the site's own badges, so alternate
  scanlation entries no longer show up as bogus chapter numbers.
- **FreeWebNovel** — the site reorganised its URLs; search, popular and latest
  now use the new endpoints and return results again.
- **Removed** three sources that no longer have a working backend:
  - **MangaFire** — its API now requires a single-use, session-bound token
    that cannot be minted outside a browser. No working mirror exists.
  - **LightNovelPub** — every mirror is either Cloudflare-blocked or has shut
    down.
  - **FlameComics** — the domain now redirects to Discord. No working mirror.

## Under the hood

- **Pack covers cleaned up** — dead `bacakomik` hosts and mis-pointed
  `manhwaindo` entries were removed from the bundled packs, and packs were
  regenerated so the affected collections point at live sources again. The pack
  refresher had been reading the wrong field off the search API and silently
  discovering no hosts, which left some collections empty; it now reads the
  aggregated host list and refills every item.
- **Fewer moving parts** — the source pickers, novel-source lists, referers and
  search-relevance rules no longer mention the retired sources.

# v1.2.15 — The App Store theme, everywhere

## The carousels finally look like the App Store

The App Store theme already had the right colours, fonts, and controls, but the
home carousels still used the old three-up grid. Now the whole layout follows
the App Store language.

## What changed

- **Carousel rails** — larger, edge-to-edge cards (~2.15 visible on a phone,
  with the next card peeking) instead of a cramped three-up row. The default
  dark and light themes keep their original sizing.
- **Carousel arrows** — the prev/next buttons stay visible on desktop and hide
  on touch devices, styled as frosted iOS glass circles.
- **Scroll indicator** — restyled as a thin iOS page indicator with a blue
  pill thumb, centred under each rail.
- **Section headers** — App Store large-title rhythm; the "View All" link is
  now Apple-blue text with a chevron instead of a tinted pill.
- **Featured cards** — the large "story" card gets rounded corners, an accent
  subtitle, and a pill Read button.
- **See-all tile** — a solid iOS card with a chevron instead of a dashed box.
- **Packs** — borderless cards with soft shadows, pill filter chips, and a
  rounded select field.
- **Novels** — the sub-tabs are now a proper segmented control.
- **Library** — history entries render as a grouped inset list with hairline
  separators.
- **Account** — stat tiles are iOS cards with system-font numbers.
- **States** — empty, error, search, and loading placeholders all use the
  theme's glass surfaces and shimmer tokens.

## Unchanged

Dark (still the default) and Light are untouched, and the App Store theme is
still opt-in under **Account → App Settings → UI Theme**. Your saved choice is
applied before the first paint, so there is no flash of the wrong theme.

# v1.2.12 — CGBUM chapters actually load

## The bug

Opening any CGBUM chapter showed blank pages. The images never arrived, so the
reader sat on placeholders no matter how long you waited.

The cause was not, as an earlier note claimed, that the image host blocks
datacenter traffic. The real reason is that CGBUM's chapter image server
(`cdn8.cgbum.com`) refuses every request that does not carry a special
`cgbum_reader_ts` cookie, which the chapter page itself hands out when it
loads. That cookie is marked HttpOnly, so the app's WebView cannot read it, and
it also expects a `cgbum.com` referer. The backend captured neither, so every
image came back rejected and the reader had nothing to show.

## The fix

- **The backend now keeps the cookie.** When it fetches a chapter page it reads
  the cookie the page sets and attaches it to each image in that chapter.
- **The image proxy forwards it — but only where it belongs.** The cookie is
  passed on only for CGBUM's own hosts, so the proxy cannot be used to leak
  cookies to arbitrary sites.
- **Offline downloads send it too.** Downloading a chapter for offline reading
  now presents the same cookie and referer, so saved chapters actually contain
  images instead of error pages.
- **Covers were never affected** and still load as before.

The result: CGBUM chapter pages load normally, in the reader and in downloads.

## Notes

- The earlier v1.2.9 note blaming datacenter IP blocking has been corrected. The
  host was reachable all along; it was waiting for the cookie.

# v1.2.11 — Updates you can actually trust

## The old updater never worked, and it was dangerous

Two problems sat underneath the update system, and neither was visible from
the outside.

The first was that updates silently did nothing. The app shipped with Capgo's
Capacitor updater enabled, but the WebView is pointed at the embedded Node
server on `http://localhost:3000`, not at the Capgo-managed bundle folder. So
Capgo could download and "activate" a new web bundle all day long and the app
would keep serving the old files from disk. Every update looked successful and
changed nothing.

The second was worse. The Node backend exposed `/api/internal/update`, which
accepted a bundle from any caller on the machine and wrote it straight into
the running app. No signature, no hash, no authentication. Anything that could
reach that port could replace the code the app runs.

Both are gone. Updates now flow through a single signed channel, and the old
unsigned endpoints have been removed entirely.

## How updates work now

- **Signed releases.** Every update is described by a manifest that lists the
  version, the download URL, the file size, and a SHA-256 hash of the bundle.
  The manifest is signed in CI with an Ed25519 key. The app carries only the
  public key and refuses anything whose signature does not verify.
- **Verified before install.** The app downloads the bundle, checks its size
  and SHA-256 against the signed manifest, rejects any archive entry that
  escapes the target directory, then installs it atomically. A bundle that
  fails any check never touches the running app.
- **Safe boots with rollback.** A new bundle gets three chances to start. If
  it throws or the app cannot confirm a clean boot, the app falls back to the
  previous version automatically. Only the three most recent bundles are kept
  on disk.
- **Honest version gates.** The feed records a minimum app version, so an
  update that needs a newer native shell is skipped rather than installed and
  broken. Downgrades and versions you have already rolled back are refused.
- **No restart guesswork.** Applying an update restarts the embedded runtime
  cleanly instead of relying on the activity to be recreated, which fixes the
  old "launch it twice" behavior.

## In the app

Account → Updates now reflects reality:

- **Check for updates** asks the signed feed, not a dead backend.
- **Install** appears only when a verified update is waiting, and shows the
  release notes for that version before you tap it.
- **Release notes** are fetched from the same feed, so the changelog you read
  matches the build that was published.

## For maintainers

- A single command publishes a release: it builds the web bundle and backend,
  zips the payload, signs the manifest, opens the GitHub release, and refreshes
  the feed. A preflight check refuses to publish unless the version matches in
  `package.json`, `app.js`, the Gradle build, and a non-empty changelog.
- The private signing key lives only in CI secrets and a local `.secrets/`
  file that is git-ignored. It is never committed.
- The publish job runs the full test suite first and stops if anything fails.

## Notes

- The legacy `backend-update.js` payload and its boot path have been removed;
  an installed copy is cleaned up on first launch.
- If you build the app yourself, run `npm run ota:keys` once to generate a
  keypair, then put the printed public key into the manifest module and keep
  the private key out of version control.
